volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CONEY ISLAND
notes: New York City's summer resort located in Brooklyn which is 10 miles from the city. Nearly 6 miles long and 1 mile wide. This is perhaps the most popular playground in the world and is visited by over 20 million persons during the summer. Here one will find all kinds of amusements that are spectacular to old as well as the young. All subways and bus lines serve this section as well as steamboats to Steeplechase Pier.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GEORGE WASHINGTON BRIDGE
notes: Spanning the Hudson to Fort Lee, N. J. It is the longest suspension bridge in the world. The length of the bridge and its approaches (including the tunnel to Amsterdam Ave.) is 12,430 ft. The span across the river is 3,500 ft. The view from this bridge is magnificent as you can view the shores of New York and the Palisades of New Jersey.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: METROPOLITAN MUSEUM OF ART
notes: Building contains 38 galleries and rooms to foster the study of fine arts and the practice of applied art. Open daily 10 A. M. to 5 P. M. except Sundays, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Years when the hours are 1 to 6 P. M. Admission Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: LA GUARDIA AIRPORT
notes: The main artery of air transportation for New York is actually located within the city limits of Long Island. Hundreds of airliners arrive and depart daily to and from all sections of the United States, South America, England and all parts of the world. Admission to the promenade deck is 10c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: STATUE OF LIBERTY
notes: Visitors admitted free 9 A.M. to 4 P.M. Oct-April, 9 A.M. to 5 P.M. May and Sept, 9 A.M. to 6 P.M. June-Aug. Boats from Pier A, Hudson River, Fare 35c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: WHITNEY MUSEUM OF AMERICAN ART
notes: Open daily 1 to 5 P.M., Sat/Sun 2 to 6 P.M. Closed Mondays, July 4th, Thanksgiving, Christmas. Admission Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: MUSEUM OF THE NUMISMATIC SOCIETY
notes: Hours: 2-5 Daily and Sundays. Closed July 16 to September 1. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: NEW YORK MUSEUM of SCIENCE and INDUSTRY
address: R. C. A. Bldg., Rockefeller Center
notes: Hours: 10 A.M. to 10 P.M. every day. Adults 25c, Children 10c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: NEW YORK BOTANICAL GARDENS
notes: Hours: 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. daily, free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: AMERICAN GEOGRAPHICAL SOCIETY
notes: Hours: 9 A.M. to 4:45 P.M. Closed Sundays and Holidays and on Saturdays during the summer.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: HAMILTON GRANGE
notes: Hours: 10-5; Saturdays 10-1. Closed Sundays and Holidays. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE THEATRICAL DISTRICT OF NEW YORK
notes: Where all of the largest and best plays are staged and produced, is located in the heart of the city.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE TRI-BOROUGH BRIDGE
notes: Connects three of the boroughs of Greater New York (Manhattan, Bronx and Queens). This bridge is 17½ miles long and is the most direct route to the N. Y. World Fair grounds site of the United Nations General Assembly.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CATHEDRAL OF ST. JOHN, THE DIVINE
notes: America's greatest church edifice. When completed it will be the largest Gothic Cathedral in the world. The seating capacity is 15,000 and room for 40,000 standing.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT NATIONAL HISTORIC SITE
notes: Dedicated as national historic one on January 15th, 1944. It comprises 33 acres. Open to visitors from Tuesday to Saturdays, inclusive and Sundays and holidays (including any holidays that fall on Monday) from 10 A. M. to 5 P. M. Admission 25c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CITY HALL
address: Broadway, Park Row and Chambers Streets
notes: Seat of government of the metropolis; can be visited by the public from 10 A. M. to 4 P. M. daily.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE GENERAL POST OFFICE
address: 31st St. to 33rd St. and from 8th to 9th Ave.
notes: Largest post office in the world; houses 18,000 employees, makes 26 collections and 3 to 4 deliveries a day.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: HOLLAND TUNNEL
address: Starts at Canal St. in New York and ends at 12th St. in Jersey City, N. J.
notes: Underwater link under the Hudson River; consists of 2 tubes, ventilated by 84 fans.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: NEW YORK ZOOLOGICAL PARK
notes: Has the greatest collection of animals in the world; occupies 264 acres. Open 10 A. M. to one-half hour before sunset. Admission free except Tues., Wed. and Thurs. Charges: Adults 10c and Children 5c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CENTRAL PARK
address: 5th Avenue and Central Park West, 59th to 110th Streets
notes: The largest park in the city; contains 862 acres, a Zoological Park and many playgrounds.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: PENNSYLVANIA STATION
address: West 31st and 33rd Sts. between 7th and 8th Aves.
notes: Main station of the Penn. system in the city; one of the finest terminals in the world.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: ELLIS ISLAND
address: Upper bay of New York harbor
notes: First landing place of the immigrant; may be visited by securing a pass from the Commissioner of Immigration.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: MUSEUM OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK
notes: Hours: 10 A. M. to 5 P. M., Sundays 1-5 P. M. Closed Tuesdays. Free except Mondays 25c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GOVERNOR'S ISLAND
address: Upper part of New York Bay
notes: Important military headquarters and headquarters of the Eastern Division of the U. S. Army. Passes required to visit from an officer at the Barge office.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE EMPIRE STATE BUILDING
notes: Tallest building in the world; 102 stories above ground, 2 stories under ground. Houses more than 25,000 tenants.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GREENWICH VILLAGE
address: West of Washington Square and south of 13th St.
notes: Famous for its nightclubs, restaurants, artist studios, antique furniture and art shops. Many are housed in old barns, lots and cellars. The Village is still a place of gay and unconventional night life.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: FRICK COLLECTION
notes: Hours: Sundays and Holidays 1-6. Closed Mondays, Decoration Day, July 4th and Christmas. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: MUSEUM OF THE AMERICAN INDIAN
notes: Hours: 2-5. Closed Sundays, Holidays and through July and August.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE HAYDEN PLANETARIUM
address: American Museum of Natural History at 81st Street and Central Park West
notes: There can be seen "The Drama of the Skies." The most interesting feature is the "Hall of the Sun," which shows the Solar System. Hours: Weekdays shows at 2, 3:30 and 8:30 P. M.; Sat. 11 A. M., 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8:30 P. M. Sundays and Holidays 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8:30 P. M. Admission Matinees 30c, evenings 40c, Children (under 17) 20c at all times.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: PIERPONT MORGAN LIBRARY
notes: Hours: Main Bldg., Tues. and Thurs., 11-4; Exhibition Room, Daily 1-5. Closed Sundays, Holidays and July 1 to Sept. 7. Free.

name: HARLEM-125th STREET and 7th AVENUE

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: ROCKEFELLER CENTER
address: between 5th and 6th Avenues at 48th to 51st Streets
notes: The largest building project ever undertaken by private capital. Occupies 12 acres. Includes R. C. A. Building, Radio City Music Hall, R. K. O. Building, Center Theatre, Le Maison, British Empire Building, Italian Building, and International Building.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: COLISTERS
notes: The Branch of the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Hours: 10-5, Sundays 1-6 P. M., closed Christmas Morning. Free except Monday and Friday 25c. Hours: 8 to dusk; Sundays and Holidays 10 to dusk; Library closed on Saturdays (July).

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: AMERICAN MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY
notes: Hours: 10 A. M. to 5 P. M. Sundays 1-5 P. M. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GRANT'S TOMB
notes: Built of granite rock and dedicated in 1897 with money raised from public subscription. Here lies the bodies of Gen. and Mrs. Ulysses S. Grant.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: HARLEM
address: between 110th and 155th Sts., bounded by Eighth, Park and Lenox Aves.
notes: The greatest Negro metropolis in the world where over 300,000 colored people live. Here you will find a city in itself: fine restaurants, taverns, nightclubs and department stores.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska

notes: New York's Oriental section. Sight seeing buses will take visitors there from Times Square. Showing the Bloody Corner at Pell and Mott Sts.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide

notes: Home grounds of the Chicago American League baseball team.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Central Manufacturing District
address: Between Ashland Ave., Morgan St., 35th St. and Pershing Road
notes: This district contains about 250 nationally known manufacturing concerns.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Union Stock Yards
address: Between Pershing Road, 47th St., Halstead St. and S. Ashland Ave.
notes: The world's famous center of the packing industry.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Chicago Historical Museum
address: Lincoln Park at Clark St. and North Ave.
notes: Admission Free Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Adler Planetarium and Astronomical Museum
address: Lake Michigan at Roosevelt Road (1200 S.)
notes: Admission Free on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday.

volume_title: The Green Book Vacation Guide: 1949
name: Parkerview Lodge

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Ghetto
address: Maxwell between Halstead and Jefferson Sts. (1320 S. - 800 W.)
notes: This market is typical of the Russian Jewish customs. Closed on Saturday-the Jewish Sabbath. Take the Roosevelt Road cars at Dearborn and Adams Sts. to Jefferson St. and walk south.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Lindbergh Beacon
address: Palmolive Building, Michigan Ave. and Walton Place (100 E. - 921 N.)
notes: This aerial beacon is considered the most powerful ever made. Presented by Col. Sperry in commemoration of Col. Lindbergh's trans-Atlantic flight.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Merchandise Mart
notes: Largest building of its kind in the world with more floor space devoted to merchandising than any other structure. Home for thousands of wholesalers and exhibitors. A magnet for merchants and buyers from every section of the map. Visitors' tours four times daily.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Navy Pier
notes: Extending 3,000 ft. into the lake. The pier is justly popular as a recreation center and lake steamer landing. During the season band concerts and dancing.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Botanical Gardens and Conservatories
address: Humbolt Park, Washington and Lincoln Parks, and Garfield Park
notes: Formal gardens at Humbolt Park. Conservatories at Washington and Lincoln Parks and rare specimens at Garfield Park. All are visited annually by millions of sightseers.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Buckingham Fountain
address: Grant Park at the foot of Congress St. (500 S.)
notes: The largest and one of the most beautiful fountains in the world. Illuminated several nights each week.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Chinatown
address: Wentworth Ave. at Cermak Road (200 W. - 2200 S.)
notes: A district inhabited almost entirely by Chinese and devoted to their business and professional needs. A Chinese city hall, stores and restaurants attract visitors.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Chicago Water Tower
address: Michigan and Chicago Aves. (100 E. - 800 N.)
notes: An old historic landmark built before the fire of 1871. Take north bound car on State St. or north bound car on Clark St. to Chicago Ave., transfer east to Michigan Ave.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Elks Memorial
address: Lake View Ave. and Diversey Parkway (400W-2800N)
notes: Open 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. every day. Admission Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Chicago Public Library
notes: 1,600,000 volumes covering every possible reader demand. A special department for the blind, representative collections in all the more commonly used foreign languages. Houses G.A.R. Memorial Hall with exhibits of Civil War relics. Admission Free daily.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: FREE CONCERTS
address: Band shell in Grant Park next to the Field Museum of Natural History
notes: Free public band and symphony concerts by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra and the Chicago Opera Orchestra. Season starts July first and continues for 67 nights. Free concerts are also offered in other large Chicago parks.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Field Museum of Natural History
notes: One of the world's greatest and most complete exhibits of Anthropology, Botany, Geology, Zoology. Collections from all over the world of the prehistoric and the modern.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Supreme Liberty Life Insurance Company
notes: Third largest Negro insurance company in America. It employs 110 people in Chicago alone.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Parkway Ballroom
notes: Located on the upper floors of the Mutual Assurance Company building.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Metropolitan Funeral Parlors
notes: Described as a monument to Negro business.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: South Center Department Store
notes: Houses the Regal Theatre, Savoy Ballroom, U.S. and state offices, and 150 professional offices; employs upward to 200 Negroes.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Regal Theatre
notes: Located within the South Center block.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Savoy Ballroom
notes: Located within the South Center block.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Field Museum of Natural History
notes: Notable Animal exhibits - Fossils - Minerals - Meteorites. Man from all ages and every clims down to races of today. Free parking space. Admission Free Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: John G. Shedd Aquarium
notes: Newest and most complete aquarium in the world. Admission Free Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays. Other days admission 25c. School children Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Museum of Science and Industry
notes: Founded by Julius Rosenwald. Extensive exhibits of the Worlds' Fairs of 1893 and 1933, also typical exhibits of a real coal mine. Admission to mine, adults 25c and children 10c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Brookfield Zoo
notes: America's most unusual zoo, patterned after those in Germany. Admission Free, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday and holidays.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Chicago Zoological Park
address: Between the Des Plaines River and Salt Creek at Brookfield
notes: 14 miles from the Chicago central business district. Admission 25c, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. Other days Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Oriental Institute (University of Chicago)
address: Corner of 58th St. and University Ave. (5800 A - 1142 E)
notes: Collections of original monuments and antiquities made by explorations in the Near East. Admission Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Art Institute of Chicago
address: Michigan Ave. at Adams St. (100 E - 200 S)
notes: Ranks among the best art galleries in the country. Admission Free, Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday and Holidays. Admission other days 25c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: United States Court House
address: Between Adams, Jackson, Clark and Dearborn (200 S - 100 W)
notes: In this building are the Federal Courts and offices and Post Office departments.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: American Furniture Mart
notes: This building is devoted exclusively to furniture and furniture display.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Chicago Stadium
notes: Largest indoor sports arean in the world.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Coliseum
notes: Auditorium seats 14,000 persons. Take south bound Cottage Grove, Indiana, Stony Island - Wabash or Thru Route No. 1 or No. 3 cars on Wabash Ave. direct to Coliseum.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Soldiers Field
notes: Take south bound Clark St. cars, except those marked Clark-Downtown or south bound cars on Wabash Ave., except cars marked Wabash-Harrison and transfer to east bound Roosevelt Road cars to terminal. Walk one block south to entrance. Address, on Lake Front at 14th St.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1949: An International Travel Guide
name: Race Track
notes: Six months racing and six real tracks. Between May 1st and October 31st. Reached by railroads, also good automobile highways. Parking spaces are available for the motorist at all tracks.

name: ATLANTIC CITY
notes: Our Nation's most famous resort city boasts a boardwalk which parallels the ocean for eight miles, on which the visitor will find shops representing the best of this country and abroad, providing anything from antique furniture to rare jewelry. Rolling chairs can be obtained, making it easier for the visitor to traverse the entire length of the boardwalk. Convention Hall, the world's largest (seating capacity 41,000) is the arena for all forms of entertainment. Bathing and the sea air are the city's main attractions. This is a year 'round resort.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: CARLSBAD CAVERNS
notes: Open all year. One of the most superb areas included in the National Park system of the United States is a series of Caverns of unusual magnificence, located in southeastern New Mexico in the foothills of the Guadalupe Mountains. This is picturesque semi-desert area, and its vegetation is of much interest to visitors. The Carlsbad Caverns are openings made by underground water in two massive rock formations, referred to as the Carlsbad and Capitan limestones, The uplifting movements that formed the Rocky Mountains also raised the Carlsbad area above sea level, approximately 200 million years ago. Over a period of years, many chambers have been formed as the result of the constant seepage of water. The most interesting thus far is the King's Palace, Queen's Chamber and Papoose Room, 829 feet below the surface. The developed portion of the Caverns only is open to the public. The bat spectacle is one of the outstanding attractions of the Caverns. Each evening at dusk, except for the migration period, millions of bats come forth from the bat cave 180 feet below the surface to fly forth, returning before the following dawn. A talk on the bats by a naturalist is given each evening before the flight begins. The region of the Carlsbad Caverns contains many interesting desert plants, some of which bloom for only a very short period leaving no trace of ever having existed. It is advisable to carry a wrap as the temperature in the Caverns remains the same 56° throughout the year. However no special clothing is necessary. Luncheon may be obtained for a moderate price, and a special day nursery service is provided near the Caverns entrance. The Caverns may be reached by train, bus or taxi. Walnut Canyon Highway leads to the Canyon. One day is needed for the tour.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE CAPITOL
notes: Visitors 9 to 4. Open till 4:30 if Congress is in session and until one-half hour after adjournment during a night session.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE SUPREME COURT BUILDING
notes: Visiting hours are 9 to 4:30; Saturday (June 15-September 15) 9 to 1.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE LIBRARY OF CONGRESS
notes: Hours are 9 to 10. Saturdays 9 to 6. Saturdays in summer 9 to 1. Sundays and holidays 2 to 10.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE TREASURY BUILDING
notes: Visiting hours 9 to 2. Saturdays 9 to 12. Bureau of Engraving and Printing is at 14th and C Street S. W., tours 8:30 to 11 a.m. and 1 to 2 p.m.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
address: Constitution and Pennsylvania Avenues, 9th and 10th Sts.
notes: Tours from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Saturdays 9:30 to 12 noon.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: MT. VERNON
notes: Admission fee 25 cents. Route via Mount Vernon Memorial Highway or Wilson Steamboat Line from 7th Street Wharves.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE NATIONAL ZOOLOGICAL PARK
notes: Open at 7:30, exhibits at 9. Feeding hours: Monkeys 9:30 a.m., 3 p.m.; Lions and tigers 1:30; Sundays excepted.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: CHRIST CHURCH
notes: President Washington's pew is preserved. Open on week days, curator on premises 9 to 6.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: GEORGETOWN
notes: Three miles west from the Capitol is reached by the Pennsylvania Avenue cars. The city was founded before Washington and is the seat of Georgetown College.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: ARLINGTON NATIONAL CEMETERY
notes: Is in Virginia on the heights of the Potomac opposite Washington. Arlington House, built in 1802 was the home of George Washington Parke Curtis and afterwards of Robert E. Lee. During the Civil War it was a hospital, and the Arlington estate was taken over by the Government for a national cemetery. The Cemetery is open all day. The building is open from 8 to 4. The tomb of the Unknown Soldier is across the roadway from the Memorial Amphitheatre.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE WHITE HOUSE
notes: The home of the President. Visitors are admitted to the corridor, east entrance, and East Room. You may visit there 10 to 2.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: LINCOLN MEMORIAL
notes: In the form of a Greek Temple of pure white marble, west of the Washington Monument. Hours 9 to 9:30.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: CORCORAN GALLERY OF ARTS
notes: Southwest of the State Department. Admission free on Thursdays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays; other days 25 cents. Hours 9 to 4:30.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: THE SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION AND NATIONAL MUSEUM
address: The Mall (bounded by B Street N. W., B Street S. W. and Seventh and Twelfth)
notes: Occupies three buildings on the Smithsonian grounds.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide
name: LINCOLN STATUE

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1950: An International Travel Guide

notes: Art Gallery and Museum open free to public from 2 to 5 p.m. daily. Closed Mondays. Fifth Ave. Bus Nos. 4, 5 and 19.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: AMERICAN MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY
notes: Free every day in the year; weekdays 10 to 5; 1 to 5 Sun. and hol. Collections illustrate the life of land and sea from all regions of the earth. 81st St. Station, 8th Ave. Subway; 8th Ave. Bus No. 10.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CATHEDRAL OF ST. JOHN THE DIVINE
notes: Estimated cost $40,000,000. It is the world's largest Gothic Cathedral. 110th St. Sta. Seventh Ave. B'way Sub.; Nos. 3, 4 Fifth Ave. Bus; Amsterdam Avt. Bus No. 11; B'way Bus.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CENTRAL PARK
address: 59th to 110th Sts. & Fifth Ave. to Central Park West
notes: Zoo in southeast corner. Fifth Ave. Bus Nos. 1 to 6, 9 & 19; Broadway-Seventh Ave. Subway to Columbus Circle; Broadway bus to 59th St.; 6th and 7th Ave. bus to 59th St.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CITY HALL
notes: Office of the Mayor. Noteworthy century-old example of Italian Renaissance Architecture. Brooklyn Bridge Station, Lexington Ave. Subway; City Hall Station of B.M.T. Subway; Broadway Bus No. 6; Madison Ave. Bus No. 1.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CHINATOWN
notes: New York's Chinese are concentrated in this area. Chatham Sq. Station of Third Ave. El.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CLOISTERS
address: Fort Tryon Park, north of George Washington Bridge
notes: Collection of medieval art. Open daily except Mondays from 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Free except on Fridays. Fifth Ave. Bus No. 4; Eighth Ave. subway 190th St.-Overlook Terrace Station.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: EMPIRE STATE OBSERVATORIES
notes: 1,250 feet above. Open 9:45 A.M. until Midnight.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: GEORGE WASHINGTON BRIDGE
address: spans the Hudson between 178th St. in Manhattan and Fort Lee, New Jersey
notes: Longest suspension span in the world except Golden Gate Bridge, California. Roadway is 12 stories or about 250 feet above the water. Total cost $60,000,000. No. 4 Fifth Ave. Bus. No toll for pedestrians.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: GOVERNOR'S ISLAND
notes: An area of 172.35 acres, many points of historical interest. Free government boats leave from the Battery every hour. South Ferry Subway Sta. B'way Bus No. 6.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: HALL OF FAME
notes: Colonnade containing bronze tablets and busts of famous Americans by eminent contemporary sculptors.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: HALL OF MOTION (N. Y. Museum of Science and Industry)
notes: A great exhibit of man's achievement in scientific and industrial fields. Open 10 A.M. to 10 P.M. daily.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: METROPOLITAN MUSEUM OF ART
notes: Open daily 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Sundays 1 to 5 P.M. Admission free. Fifth Ave. Buses Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4. Madison Ave. Bus Nos. 1, 2. Lexington Avenue Subway to 86th St. Station.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: MUSEUM OF CITY OF NEW YORK
notes: Charming Georgian building housing various phases of New York life from its earliest beginnings to the contemporary scene. Open weekdays except Mondays, from 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Sundays, 1 P.M. to 5 P.M. Holidays, 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Free at all times. Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 Fifth Ave. Buses; 103d St. Station Lexington Ave. Subway; Madison Ave. Bus Nos. 1 and 2.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: ROCKEFELLER CENTER (and Radio City)
address: Fifth to Sixth Aves., 48th to 51st Sts.
notes: World's greatest office, shop and amusement center under one ownership.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: RADIO CITY
notes: broadcasting headquarters for National Broadcasting Company. Guided tours leave at frequent intervals every day in the year. Each tour takes one hour and includes the NBC Studios and Television.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: STATUE OF LIBERTY
notes: Boats lv. Battery, Mon. through Sun. every hr. on the hr. 9 a.m.-4 p.m. (IRT 7th Ave. to South Ferry; IRT Lex. Ave. to Bowling Green; BMT to Whitehall St.)

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: UNITED NATIONS
address: Manhattan Island, 42nd to 48th Streets; between 1st Avenue and the East River
notes: Visitors are always welcome; all but a few of the meeting places are open to the public. Admission FREE. Free tickets are issued upon request to the Council, Commission or other bodies in session. Guided Tours through thes Headquarters Building and other exhibits; a small fee is charged. Buildings are open at 9 A.M. Can be reached by the 42nd Street bus.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: TRINITY CHURCH
notes: The present building is the third on this site and dates from Ascension Day, May 21, 1846. In the Vestry Room of Trinity Church is a Tablet and Bust of Alexander Hamilton, and his body lies in the cemetery of the Church. Open to visitors 8 A.M. to 5 P.M. daily. I.R.T. 7th Ave and Lexington Ave. Subways, Wall St. Stations.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Atlanta University
notes: The graduate center of the Atlanta group of colleges. Extensive collection of books and art on Negro culture in the Trevor Arnett Library, including the Hale Woodruff murals.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Benedict College
notes: A liberal arts college and school of theology. Points of interest: Antisdel Athletic Field, the new Dining Hall-Dormitory and Osborn Hall, oldest building on the campus.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Bennett College
notes: A woman's college of arts and sciences. Of interest: Annie Merner Pfeiffer Chapel, historic Bennett Bell, the Little Theatre, the Children's House.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Bethune-Cookman College
notes: A center of culture in the deep South. Sunday community programs open to visitors, 27 modern buildings on 169 acres. Founder Mary McLeod Bethune buried on campus.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Bishop College
notes: Point of interest: The C. H. Maxson Administration Building, a fine old mansion erected before the Civil War.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Clark College
notes: A co-educational member of the Atlanta University system. Point of interest: Merrill J. Holmes Hall, modern woman's dormitory.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Dillard University
notes: A 62-acre campus two miles northeast of New Orleans business district. Architecture a combination of Georgian and modified classic. Point of interest: the Flint-Goodridge Hospital.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Fisk University
notes: National reputation as a liberal arts college of high standing. Of special interest: the Alfred Stieglitz Collection of Art, the Carl Van Vechten Art Gallery, the Aaron Douglas Murals and the Balridge Collection of African Drawings in the Erastus Milo Cravath Memorial Library. Overnight visitors may reserve accommodations through Comptroller's Office.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Gammon Theological Seminary
notes: The Divinity School of the Atlanta University system. Points of interest: "Magnolia Drive," Gammon Hall, the Anna E. Hall dormitory.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Hampton Institute
notes: A 74-acre campus on the shores of historic Hampton Roads. Of special interest: the Collis P. Huntington Memorial Library with famed collection of books and pamphlets on Negro culture, the Henry O. Tanner paintings on religious themes, Ogden Hall, the modern Bemis Laboratories, Harkness Hall. Robert Russa Moton is buried here. Holly Tree Inn provides guest accommodations.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Huston-Tillotson College
notes: Formed by the merger of the two colleges of the Congregational and Methodist Churches. In process of developing a new modern campus.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Johnson C. Smith University
notes: 22 buildings on 75 acres. Points of interest: Biddle Hall, the James B. Duke Memorial Hall, the Henry Lawrence McCrorey Building, the Jane M. Smith Memorial Church.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Knoxville College
notes: Founded in 1863. Of special interest: the Young Memorial Fine Arts Building, the Giffen-Alumni Memorial Building.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Lane College
notes: Established in 1884 to serve youth of the C. M. E. Church. Named for its founder, Bishop Isaac Lane.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: LeMoyne College
notes: Established before the close of the Civil War. Of interest: Brownlee Hall, Arthur Bruce Hall.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Lincoln University
notes: The oldest private Negro college. Established 1854. Of special interest: the Susan Reynolds Underhill Collection of African Art, Ashmun Hall (1856), Lincoln Hall (1866), the Vail Memorial Library. The Ladies Auxiliary Guest House provides overnight accommodations.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Livingstone College
notes: A campus of 316 acres. Of special interest: Hood Theological Seminary, Harris Hall. First president, Joseph Charles Price, buried here.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Morehouse College
notes: The men's college of the Atlanta University system. Of special interest: John Hope Monument, Graves Hall.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Morris Brown College
notes: A co-educational member of the Atlanta University system. Founded under patronage of the African Methodist Episcopal Church.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Paine College
notes: A winter-resort climate. Of special interest: Hoisey Hall, the Warren A. Candler Memorial Library.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Philander Smith College
notes: One of the oldest Negro colleges west of the Mississippi. Of interest: Old Budlong Hall, the modern science hall. Guest House accommodations available.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: St. Augustine's College
notes: Small campus. Points of interest: St. Agnes Hospital Training School for Nurses, Bishop Tuttle School of Social Work, St. Augustine's Chapel, Benson Library, Atkinson Hall.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Shaw University
notes: Rich historic associations. Of special interest: Shaw Hall (1871), Estey Hall (1873), the Administration Building, the Art Gallery, Women's Recreation Building. Guest accommodations available in dormitories.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Spelman College
notes: The first college for Negro women in America. Point of interest: Sisters Chapel seating 1200 with three-manual pipe organ.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Talladega College
notes: Oldest college for Negroes in Alabama established 1867. Points of interest: the Hale Woodruff Murals in Savery Library, the Henry S. DeForest Chapel.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Texas College
notes: Located 100 miles east of Dallas. Of special interest: the Home Management House, Teacher's Aid Laboratory, Tea House with dining accommodations for visitors.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Tougaloo Southern Christian College
notes: A beautiful, rolling, wooded campus four miles north of Jackson. Points of interest: "The Mansion," built as planter's residence before Civil War. now home of president; Sarah A. Dickey Memorial Infirmary.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Tuskegee Institute
notes: Magnificent campus, 157 buildings on 4,925 acres. Of special interest: the George Washington Carver Museum, famed Booker T. Washington Monument, the Infantile Paralysis Pavilion of the John A. Andrews Hospital. Booker T. Washington and George Washington Carver buried on campus.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Virginia Union University
notes: The Belgian Friendship Building on the campus is a gift from the Belgian Government. Points of interest: the Robert L. Vann Tower, the William J. Clarke Library. Friday visitors may attend weekly campus convocations.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Wiley College
notes: Landscaped campus of 46 acres. Points of interest: The Sunken Garden, Brainard Chapel.

volume_title: Travelguide 1957
name: Xavier University
notes: A Catholic university, "New Xavier," was founded in 1915. Of special interest: three outstanding English Gothic structures of Indiana limestone, collection of French language books donated by the French government, and the Edward Morrell Memorial Collection of Bronzes.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Statue of Liberty
notes: Bartholdi's huge female figure of 'Liberty Enlightening the World,' presented to the United States by France in 1885. Figure, 151 ft. tall, tops 142 ft. pedestal. The copper statue alone weighs 225 tons. Circular stairway of 168 steps leads to interior of head. Boat to island leaves Pier A, Battery Place on the hour daily.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Fraunces Tavern
notes: Early Georgian colonial architecture. Museum of Revolutionary relics on second floor. Open 10-4 Mon. to Fri., 10-3 Sat. except during summer.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Wall Street
notes: The great financial center. At Nassau and Wall is Sub-Treasury Building on site of Federal Hall where George Washington took oath as first President of the United States. Admission free.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: United Nations World Capital
address: Along the East River, north of 42d St.
notes: Houses the Secretariat which is the 3,000-employee administrative organ of the United Nations, staffed by international civil servants. Meeting place of the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council and Trusteeship Council. For guided tour consult the Admissions Office.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: CHINA TOWN
notes: A short walk from City Hall and Brooklyn Bridge. Joss houses, curio shops and Chinese restaurants.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: ROOSEVELT HOUSE
notes: Birthplace and boyhood home of Theodore Roosevelt. Contains a collection of mementos of the President. Open weekdays, except Mon., 10-5; Sun. and holidays. Free.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: TIMES SQUARE
address: Intersection of Broadway, Seventh Ave. and 42nd St.
notes: Often called the “Great White Way” because of the brilliant “spectaculars,” flashing theatre marquees, shops, hotels and restaurants.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: EMPIRE STATE BUILDING
notes: Tallest structure in the world; 102 stories; 1,472 ft. high; 67 elevators. Observation terraces on 86th and 102d floors. Open 9:45 to midnight. Admission.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: ROCKEFELLER CENTER
address: 48th to 51st Streets between Fifth Avenue and Avenue of the Americas
notes: City-within-a-city. 15 skyscraper buildings occupy 12½ acres. Take a guided tour.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: CENTRAL PARK
address: 59th to 110th Sts., Fifth Avenue to Central Park West
notes: 2½ miles long, ½ mile wide. Contains the Mall, Zoo and Wollman Memorial; Central Park Lake with boats for hire; Cleopatra’s Needle. Horse drawn hacks may be hired for about $3.00 for the first half hour and $1 for every hour thereafter. Starting point 59th St. and Fifth Ave.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: HAYDEN PLANETARIUM
notes: “Theatre of the Stars” portrays the wonders of the sky. Performances daily. Admission charged.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: GRANT'S TOMB
notes: Massive granite memorial overlooking Hudson River containing the remains of General and Mrs. U. S. Grant.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Riverside Church
notes: Inter-denominational church resembles the 13th Century Cathedral of Chartres, France. The carillon, largest in the world, is housed at the top of a 22-story tower. The late Henry Burleigh was a featured vocalist there.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Coney Island
notes: Internationally known playground on Atlantic Ocean with 5 miles of bathing beach, boardwalk and amusements. Take BMT subway.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Bronx Zoo
address: Pelham Parkway & Bronx River Parkway Extension
notes: Largest in kinds and number of specimens in America. Contains a special zoo for children who are permitted to play with tame animals. Admission.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Hall of Fame
notes: The uptown campus of New York University is identified by the Hall of Fame. Contains eighty-three bronze busts and tablets of outstanding Americans. Booker T. Washington, the only Negro, was elected May, 1946. Sidney Barthe was the sculptor.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Jones Beach
notes: Reached via Meadowbrook and Wantagh State Parkways. From Harlem over the Triborough Bridge past La Guardia Airport. Features bathing in the Atlantic Ocean, Zachs Bay.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Franklin D. Roosevelt's Home
notes: Birthplace and burial site of the 32d President. Includes the Rose Garden and the Roosevelt Memorial Library (erected 1939).

name: Entry Fees and Equipment
notes: Tourist entering Canada are not required to pay entry fees, and may bring with them such articles of tourist outfits or sportsmen's equipment as they may require while in Canada for their own use and not for gain or hire, upon reporting same to the Customs Officer at the Canadaian frontier port of entry.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: Entering and Touring Mexico
notes: The only requirement is a simple permit issued at a cost of three pesos by the Mexican customs upon crossing the border at Nuevo Laredo. This permit may also be obtained in Laredo, Texas, at the branch office of the A. A. A. at the corner of Matamoros St. and Convent Ave. Your car registration certificate is necessary for purpose of identification. No special driving license is required other than on issued to you by your particular state; this you should keep in your car or on your person at all times when driving in Mexico.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: NOTE
notes: Do not discard any car equipment while in Mexico—such as old tires, broken bumpers, etc.,—or you will probably be required to pay duty on such missing items upon leaving Mexico.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: DRIVING PRECAUTIONS
notes: All road signs are in Spanish. If you cannot get a folder and do not understand the meaning of a road sign, check your speed there is something ahead which requires attention, because most highways in Mexico are not fenced and livestock is often found on the road; therefore excessive driving speeds around curves or places where the view is obstructed is very dangerous. In the mountain region, especially between Tamazunchale and Zimapan, heavy fogs are occasionally encountered. When the atmosphere becomes so dense that vision ahead is obscured it is wise to pull off to the side of the road as far as possible and wait with your lights on for a few minutes for the fog to lift.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: HOTELS
notes: First class hotels may be found everywhere in Mexico along the travel routes. Prices are reasonable. Excellent food in both American and European style can be obtained practically everywhere.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: MEXICAN CUSTOMS REGULATIONS
notes: Visitors entering Mexico as tourist may bring in any reasonable amount of clothing, sporting goods camping outfits, cameras, forty packages of cigarette, 100 cigars or a pound of tobacco free of duty. Upon arrival at the Custom Office, all baggage must be removed from the car for inspection. (Registered porters will do this work for you for a small tip.) Most of the attendants speak english so you will have no difficulty. If you have your Tourist Card and auto permit, there are no cost of any kind. These formalities are completed in a few minutes.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: U. S. CUSTOMS REGULATIONS
notes: You are permitted to bring back merchandise up to a value of $100.00, free of duty, when intended for personal use or gifts, others may be imported only upon payments of duty, because of patent and trade-mark restrictions, however the exceptions are rare, yet a few brands of perfume are included in this category, if you intend to purchase perfume it is best to buy at reliable stores familiar with the U. S. customs requirement. Importation of liquors under the $100.00 exemption are limited to a one gallon. Residents of dry states cannot bring in liquor. Texas residents one quart. Certain other states have regulatory laws and taxes affecting all liquors brought into such states. If you intend to bring back liquor with you, it is best to check the liquor regulations of your own state before leaving.

volume_title: Smith's tourist guide of necessary information for businessman, tourist, traveler and vacationist
name: SPECIAL NOTE
notes: Should you carry with you into Mexico any articles of foreign make, such as cameras, binoculars, or any articles of unusual value, or whose origin cannot easily be proved they should be recorded at the U. S. Customs Office in Laredo, before you enter Mexico. A certificate listing such articles will be given you, without charge, which will protect you against argument or payment of duty upon your return to the United States.
